title: Onset kinetics on a resolved neighbour cell: where a whole-cell threshold and a local one disagree
description:
A pre-registered pilot study. A published two-cell study (doi:10.5281/zenodo.23253738) solved the neighbour of a failing LG M50 cell twice with identical inputs, as a single temperature (lumped) and as a resolved three-dimensional field, and compared both with fixed onset temperatures. This study replaces the fixed temperatures with the B-CRNN decomposition kinetics of Koenig, Zhao and Deng (Chemical Engineering Journal 507 (2025) 160402), integrated along the archived histories of the resolved hottest node, the resolved mean and the lumped node: the posterior-mean model passively (Stage 1, 49 cases) and as a heat source in both models (Stage 2, reactive and one-way, five cases); 200 joint draws of the kinetic posterior and 30 Latin hypercube draws of the roll's published thermal properties (Stage 3); and each of the posterior's three submodels varied alone over the same draws, the other two at their posterior mean (Stage 4, version 1.1.0). Stage 5 (version 1.2.0) sets both neighbours, with the cans in contact and joined by welded tabs, against the measured two-cell propagation tests of Fransson et al. (Journal of Power Sources 617 (2024) 234916, CC BY 4.0). Conduction and radiation only between the cells: venting, ejecta and flame are excluded. Stages 1 to 4 concern onset in a neighbour; Stage 5 asks whether the neighbour propagates. Each stage's predictions were committed and pushed before its kinetics ran on an archived history (commits b09ef1d and 2657aee), Stage 4's before any grouped run (a975f20), and Stage 5's before any Stage 5 run (b4883ba).

Results

  • With copper busbars (500 mW/K in all) and the largest Battery Failure Databank energy (33.2 kJ), the resolved hottest node starts to self-heat at 0.15 K/min 23.4 s and 26.4 s before the lumped node (4.2 against 27.6 s for a 10 s release, 11.5 against 37.9 s for 30 s). Under the posterior-mean kinetics every start is a fresh SEI decomposing at 108.4 C.
  • The smallest busbar conductance at which only the local chemistry starts is 100 mW/K under the posterior-mean kinetics (21.5 kJ); across the kinetic posterior it spreads over six of the seven conductances from 5 to 500 mW/K.
  • With the reaction heat fed back, the hottest node enters the internal-short band (255.7 C) at the same moment as without it, so the entry is set by conduction. The lumped cell never enters the band, yet releases 6.0 and 7.1 times the resolved cell's reaction heat.
  • Over 200 draws of the kinetic posterior the lumped node never starts before the hottest node, in any of the 42 two-strip cases. At 33.2 kJ, 30 s and 500 mW/K the lead runs from 15.4 to 58.9 s (2.5 to 97.5 %, median 26.3 s); 36.5 % of the draws start below 100 C, by SEI decomposition.
  • At that case, over the published spread of the roll's conductivity and heat capacity (contact, busbar and emissivity held fixed), the hottest node's onset varies 0.027 times as much as over the kinetic posterior and the lumped node's 0.11 times (standard deviations): the kinetics set both onsets.
  • The anode-electrolyte submodel, which holds the SEI decomposition, carries essentially all of the lead's variance. Varied alone it gives 0.997 of the lead's variance over the joint draws at 33.2 kJ, 30 s and 500 mW/K (paired bootstrap 0.92 to 1.09), and 0.89 to 1.09 of every output's at 500 and 100 mW/K; the NCM811 cathode gives 0.000 and the separator 0.001 to 0.002. Exploratory analysis shows that the separator's melting still decides the mode of 13 marginal draws. With it at its posterior mean no draw starts below 100 C, against 37.5 % with it varied.
  • Restricting the anode-electrolyte submodel to the half of its particles closest to the posterior mean (a parameter-space proxy for a tighter posterior) narrows the lead's 2.5 to 97.5 % interval only from 43.5 to 37.1 s (14.6 %; 18.1 % when the half is chosen on the SEI decomposition's own parameters). Exploratory analysis, written after the results, traces this to the lead's two modes (hottest-node starts by 122.4 C, or at 184.9 C and above), both of which a tighter posterior keeps.
  • Stage 5: the tests propagated in 9 of 16, at 147 to 342 s. With a steel-on-steel line contact of 200, 2,000 and 3,700 W/(m2 K) (a textbook table's range, so every result is conditional on it), welded tabs bracketed by the two-cell study's nickel strip, and 33.2 kJ at an assumed 100 % state of charge, neither neighbour reaches 255.7 C within 900 s in any of 5,248 runs, which cover all 200 kinetic draws. In the central case (central contact and tabs) the resolved hot spot, on the line of contact, peaks at 191.5 to 192.3 C and the lumped neighbour at 159.4 to 162.1 C; the highest peaks of any run are 226.7 C (resolved) and 180.6 C (lumped). The model was expected to propagate later than the tests, if at all, because it lacks their venting, ejecta and flame; it does not propagate at all within 900 s.
  • Scorecards. Stages 1 and 2: P1 to P4 held; P5(a) held, against the registered expectation; P5(b) failed; P5(c) held. Stage 3: P1, P2 and P5 held; P3, P4 and P6 failed. Stage 4: P1, P2, P3 and P5 held; P4 failed. Stage 5: P2 held, because the lumped neighbour never propagates; P1 and P6 failed; P3, P4, P5 and P7 were not met, and so failed, because no run propagated.

Checks. The source's DSC curves are reproduced. An emulation of its ARC test gives T_in = 179.3 C with the posterior-mean kinetics, inside its two-sigma band (169.0 to 198.0 C), but T_on = 199.8 C at its stated 1 C/min trigger, below its band (255.7 to 302.1 C). Over the 200 kinetic draws the same emulation failed the brief's acceptance (the 2.5 and 97.5 percentiles of the main-cluster T_in at 146.3 and 191.4 C); after the failure was reported the author amended the check (the paper's own mean plus and minus two standard deviations, measured from the emulation's own T_in), under which it passes; both verdicts are recorded. Halving tolerances, steps and grids moves the onsets by at most 7e-5 of themselves; energy accounts close to 1e-11 of the heat taken in at the published conductivities; with a 1e4 W/mK roll the resolved and lumped models agree within 0.8 K. Before the Stage 4 predictions, the grouped models were shown to separate exactly by submodel, and the posterior-mean model and five joint draws run through the Stage 4 path reproduce Stages 1 and 3 exactly. Before the Stage 5 predictions, every contact and tab path matched the lumped formula to 2e-16 and an analytic steady case to 5e-5 of the rise, and the Stage 5 code in the two-cell configuration reproduced Stages 1 and 2; in Stage 5, halving the mesh spacing or the steps changes the central case's peak rise by at most 0.31 %, the energy accounts close to 8.4e-12 of the heat taken in, the 48 runs made on both machines agree to 1.6e-10 J and 2.9e-11 K, and an independent read of every registered number and verdict reproduced them all, and the nine discrepancies it found in the draft texts were corrected.

Limits. Kinetics from other cells (NCM811 and graphite DSC data, the source cell's reactant fractions) with a fresh SEI; Stage 3 treats the posterior's three submodels as independent, and its thermal ranges are literature spreads (O'Regan et al. 2022; Chen et al. 2021), not measured uncertainties of this cell; Stage 4 holds two submodels at their posterior mean, and its central half is a parameter-space proxy for a tighter posterior, not a simulated measurement; Stage 1 ignores the reaction heat and Stage 2 is one-way; conduction and radiation only; Stages 1 to 4 use one geometry without the cap and tabs; Stage 5's contact conductance is a textbook range for steel on steel, its tabs a bracket from the two-cell study, its state of charge assumed, and it has no venting, ejecta or flame.
